question: where do the stable cells behind the reported DoD tilt come from, and is the tilt a property of the tile or of that population and of the registration?

inputs.role: pipeline corrections: grid geometry, per-swath constants, geoid datum (const + tilt), drift curves
DoD under audit: gen2 at the cover-dependent percentile minus gen1's registered median, m, + = elevation rose
gen2 gridded ground, the DoD reference surface, m
PyForestScan canopy cover from the gen2 cloud, plant-area based, min_height 2 m
floodplain cells, excluded from the population
agricultural region: penetration >= 0.45, eroded 6 cells off the cover boundary, channel buffer removed (analysis/ridgelines/hillslope_regions_K.py)
per-return gen1 CSF ground offsets to the gen2 surface, slope-normal mm, with the four registration terms and point_source_id / gps_time / scan_angle per return

params.name: cover_max
params.why: the population under audit was defined with this ceiling

params.name: block_m ladder
params.why: 50 m is the repo default used by offset_vs_angle.py and cover_offset_regression.py; the larger blocks are added because the semivariogram measured in section 2c shows the residual field is still correlated at 400 m, so a 50 m block treats correlated cells as independent. Nothing is excluded by this; it changes only the reported SE.

params.name: map_block_m
params.why: the coverage map was asked for in 250 m blocks

params.name: n_boot
params.why: block-bootstrap replicates, used only to check the sandwich SE against the bootstrap the original claim quoted. No data are dropped.

params.name: n_elev_bins
params.why: equal-count elevation bins via binstats.quantile_edges, which spans the full observed range so no elevation is truncated. The count sets resolution only.

params.name: z_split
params.why: the antimode of the population's OWN elevation histogram (5 m bins), used only to name the two limbs the data already show; every fit is also reported over equal-count elevation bins spanning the full range, which uses no threshold.

masks.name: stable open cells under audit
masks.defn: refcells.reference_cells() at repo defaults, then canopy_cover_pfs <= 0.02, floodplain_mask removed, finite dod_cover_q2.npy

columns.what: the quantity or subset the row describes
columns.n: cells (or cell-flightline rows, where stated) entering the fit
columns.blocks: independent spatial blocks the fit's cluster-robust SE counts
columns.mean_mm: mean DoD in the band, mm (+ = elevation rose)
columns.mean_se: cluster-robust standard error of mean_mm, mm
columns.dE: fitted easting gradient of the DoD, mm per km east
columns.dE_se: cluster-robust standard error of dE, mm/km
columns.dN: fitted northing gradient of the DoD, mm per km north
columns.dN_se: cluster-robust standard error of dN, mm/km
columns.dE_lad: the same easting gradient from a least-absolute-deviations fit, mm/km
columns.dN_lad: the same northing gradient from a least-absolute-deviations fit, mm/km
columns.block_m: size of the spatial block the cluster-robust SE is computed over, m
columns.coef: fitted coefficient in the units named by term
columns.model: the set of regressors fitted jointly
columns.z_term: coefficient on gen2 ground elevation z_after, mm per 100 m of elevation
columns.d_term: coefficient on distance to the nearest floodplain cell, mm per km
columns.ag_term: coefficient on the agricultural-region mask, mm (ag minus non-ag)
columns.lag_lo: lower edge of the separation-distance bin, m
columns.lag_hi: upper edge of the separation-distance bin, m
columns.pairs: randomly drawn cell pairs in the lag bin
columns.gamma_rms: sqrt of the semivariance in the bin, mm (the rms difference / sqrt2)
columns.rho: implied correlation 1 - gamma/variance of the residual field
columns.rows: cell-flightline ground estimates for that line on the stable cells
columns.E_span: easting extent of that line's stable cells, km -- its leverage on dE
columns.h_m: fitted flying height from x = a + b*y + h*tan(scan) within the line, m; the sign alternates because scan_angle is body-fixed and the aircraft turns
columns.dir: corr(gps_time, northing) within the line: -1 = flown south, +1 = flown north
columns.mm_per_s: OLS slope of the DoD on gps_time within the line, mm per second of mission time -- a residual along-track drift alternates its sign in northing between lines, a ground-fixed field does not
columns.c_tan: dE re-expressed in the line's own body frame, mm per unit tan(scan) (= dE * h): the across-track coefficient this line's easting gradient would imply
columns.elev_lo: lower edge of the elevation bin, m
columns.elev_hi: upper edge of the elevation bin, m
columns.median_mm: median DoD in the bin, mm
columns.band_lo: lower edge of the northing band, m above the tile's southern limit
columns.band_hi: upper edge of the northing band, m
columns.removed: which registration term was subtracted back out before refitting
columns.p0: minimum elevation of the population, m
columns.p100: maximum elevation of the population, m

notes: elba_fulldensity reference_cells cuts: start=355600, not a divide cell=243595, |curv| > 0.015=12788, slope >= 12 deg=37771, building returns=116, clear-cut (frac drop > 0.3)=1160, blufftop retreat margin=2738, |DoD| > 500 mm=376, kept=57056
headline: the easting tilt is landform, not registration: dE -14.19 mm/km tile-wide becomes +3.51 +- 6.55 on the upland limb; the northing tilt survives every control at -17.90 +- 3.90 mm/km (250 m blocks) and is NOT along-track drift (its sign in gps_time alternates with flight direction while its sign in northing does not)
